findings.journey: Reopen the exact calculation used before a later refund or cost revision
findings.expected: If historical calculation review is offered, earlier metrics and complete input lineage can be reconstructed; otherwise explicitly document that only current projections are supported.
findings.actual: The supported authority overwrites one calculation row per scope/version. A later refund keeps the ID but changes metrics; the list is current projections, not immutable versions. Lineage lists event IDs but not the cost evidence used. This is a missing workflow, not a broken existing immutable-history contract. The final test validates the actual mutable contract.
findings.business_impact: A seller cannot reconstruct the exact earlier profitability calculation from this projection alone, even though source events remain persisted.
findings.suggested_fix: Define whether retained calculation versions are required; reuse canonical snapshot/audit patterns and include applicable cost/source identities. Do not relabel current projections as immutable history.

findings.journey: Turn an advisory signal into an explicitly reviewed supported action
findings.expected: Distinguish signal acknowledgement from a durable canonical HUMAN approval; do not claim approval or execution where only an advisory response exists.
findings.actual: The request-action authority returns approval_required and says the recommendation is recorded, but it adds no durable approval/action record. There is no approve/reject/failed-execution/retry lifecycle in this authority. The default-deny external boundary is working and was not bypassed.
findings.business_impact: A first-time seller may mistake a requested or acknowledged signal for a saved authorization or completed action.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify messaging and route only supported actions to their existing canonical HUMAN authorities; do not add a duplicate approval system or expose remote execution in QA.

findings.journey: Create a first stock record from the inventory empty state
findings.expected: An inventory empty state gives a supported UI path to create the canonical item before adjustments, reservations and channel mapping.
findings.actual: The workspace tells the seller to create a product stock record, but exposes filters, adjustments, ledger and mapping only for existing items. Its canonical creation API exists; this suite seeds it through that API. Product master inventory fields are a separate model and are not a demonstrated replacement for this missing handoff.
findings.business_impact: API fixtures can exercise populated inventory, but a first-time seller can still encounter a UI onboarding dead end.
reproduction_steps: Inspect the empty state and controls in unified-inventory.component.ts
Compare POST /api/v1/inventory/items with MarketplaceService UI callers.
findings.suggested_fix: Plan an explicit canonical creation/handoff using the existing API, with opening balance provenance and HUMAN review. Do not duplicate stock ledgers.

findings.actual: 85 rule/state incomplete occurrences across recorded routes; see the exact targets in phase-4-accessibility.json. These are manual-review requirements, not confirmed violations or independent code defects.

findings.business_impact: Automated evidence does not establish accessibility of every table, conditional control or assistive-technology interaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Independently review remaining nodes and assistive navigation; add bounded regressions for confirmed defects. Do not disable rules or equate empty/offscreen checks with success.
